---
title: "Download the data"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, comment = "#>")
library(jnanalytics)
parquet_dir <- file.path("..", "..", "parquet")
base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/main/parquet/"
release <- as.data.frame(arrow::read_parquet(file.path(parquet_dir, "release.parquet")))
```

The reference tables and journal-level aggregates are published as
[Parquet](https://parquet.apache.org/) files with every release. They are kept
in the [`parquet/`](https://github.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/tree/main/parquet)
folder of the repository and can be read without an account or API key, in R,
Python, DuckDB or any other tool that reads Parquet. Article-level tables
(`articles`, `article_first_authors`, `article_agreements`) are only in
BigQuery, `subugoe-collaborative.jn_analytics`.

Data and code are released under CC0.

## Current release

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Item = c(
      "Version", "Built", "Crossref snapshot", "OpenAlex snapshot",
      "JCT snapshot", "Publication years"
    ),
    Value = c(
      release$version, format(release$snapshot_date), release$crossref_snapshot,
      release$openalex_snapshot, release$jct_snapshot,
      paste(release$pub_year_min, release$pub_year_max, sep = "–")
    )
  )
)
```

The links below always point to the latest release. Earlier releases are in
the [history of `parquet/`](https://github.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/commits/main/parquet).

## Files

```{r}
tables <- c(jn_publish_tables(), "release")
files <- paste0(tables, ".parquet")
paths <- file.path(parquet_dir, files)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(paths)))
rows <- vapply(paths, function(p) nrow(arrow::open_dataset(p)), numeric(1))
size_mb <- file.size(paths) / 1e6
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Table = paste0("[`", tables, "`](data-model.html#", gsub("_", "-", tables), ")"),
    Rows = format(rows, big.mark = ","),
    Size = ifelse(size_mb < 0.1, "< 0.1 MB", sprintf("%.1f MB", size_mb)),
    Download = paste0("[", files, "](", base_url, files, ")")
  ),
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "l")
)
```

Every table and column is described in the [data model](data-model.html),
including the counting rules. Two matter most when working with the files:

- Counts can be summed over journals, years and work types; compute shares
  from the sums. Filter `work_type` to `article` and `review` for research
  articles.
- The country tables count a work once per first-author country (full
  counting). Take totals from `journal_year`, never by summing over countries.

## Usage

### R, with jnanalytics

Download all files into one folder and use the analysis functions:

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
library(jnanalytics)

base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/main/parquet/"
files <- paste0(c(jn_publish_tables(), "release"), ".parquet")
dir.create("jn_parquet")
for (f in files) {
  download.file(paste0(base_url, f), file.path("jn_parquet", f), mode = "wb")
}

src <- jn_source("jn_parquet")
jn_oa(src, by = c("pub_year", "oa_model"))
```

### R, with arrow

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
download.file(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/main/parquet/journal_year.parquet",
  "journal_year.parquet", mode = "wb"
)
journal_year <- arrow::read_parquet("journal_year.parquet")
```

### Python

```python
import pandas as pd

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/main/parquet/journal_year.parquet"
journal_year = pd.read_parquet(url)
```

### DuckDB

DuckDB reads the files directly from their URL:

```sql
SELECT pub_year, oa_model,
       sum(articles) AS articles,
       sum(articles_oa) / sum(articles) AS share_oa
FROM 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/main/parquet/journal_year.parquet'
WHERE work_type IN ('article', 'review')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL;
```

## Column descriptions in the files

Each file carries its column descriptions as JSON in the Parquet metadata
(`jn_columns`), together with the table name (`jn_table`) and the package
version (`jn_version`):

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
meta <- arrow::open_dataset("journal_year.parquet")$schema$metadata
jsonlite::fromJSON(meta$jn_columns)
```
